title: Los mangos
desc: Fruit falls on the roof for a month
setting: A mango hits your roof at six in the morning. Don Beto is on the pavement laughing at you.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.en: Ideay, chele, did the mango wake you up?

options.es: Me despertó, don Beto. Pensé que era un ladrón.
options.en: It woke me up, don Beto. I thought it was a thief.
options.feedback: You took the joke and added to it. He will be telling that one for a week.
True and clear. You let a joke go by without giving anything back.
To him that tree is fruit for free. You have complained about a gift.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Ya vas a ver. Todo abril es así.
steps.en: You will see. All April is like that.

options.es: ¿Y qué hace uno con tanto mango?
options.en: And what does one do with so many mangos?
options.feedback: The useful question. April gives you more mango than anybody can eat and everyone has an answer.
You have taken the news and dropped the conversation.

options.en: I am going to cut down the tree.
options.feedback: Say that on this street and you will be remembered for it.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Se come verde con sal. Probá.
steps.en: You eat it green with salt. Try it.

options.en: Green? I have never eaten it like that.
options.feedback: Surprise, honestly said, which invites him to teach you. That is what he was after.

options.en: All right, I will try it.
options.feedback: Willing, which is the main thing. A little flat.
Where you come from. Here green with salt is half the point of April.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Con sal y vinagre. Vas a ver que te gusta.
steps.en: With salt and vinegar. You will see that you like it.

options.es: Si usted lo dice, don Beto, yo le creo.
options.en: If you say so, don Beto, I believe you.
options.feedback: Warm, respectful, and it hands him the last word, which is his by age.
You have closed off the whole thing over one ingredient.
